messages:
Jorge: quick proposal — add a small 'routing rationale' column to the request-trace table in Console. Right now we only show model + region; we should surface: customer tier, policy rule that matched, and any fallback variant applied.
Mina: +1. We need to be careful about volume. This should rely on existing routing headers instead of a new RPC.
Toby: do we have the headers today for every request? I thought we only persisted model id and region in traces.
Mina: we log these headers at the edge already: 
```
X-Redwood-Tier: enterprise
X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1
X-Redwood-Routing-Policy: cost-priority
X-Redwood-Model-Variant: rwv-1-q4
X-Redwood-Fallback-Reason: capacity || latency
```
but we only sample them for the free tier. enterprise customers get full traces.
Kendra: UX idea — show a compact badge sequence in the table row: [tier] [region] [variant] and a small ? hover that expands the policy evaluation chain (e.g., matched rule #42 -> capacity check fail -> fallback to rwv-1-q4). Keep it one-click to 'playback' the routing path using the stored decision events.
ConsoleUX-Bot: mockup attached (inline): compact badges, hover tooltip + 'playback' icon that opens a side panel with step-by-step policy decisions and timestamps. Also include a link to the raw trace id.
Jorge: good. Two implementation Qs: (1) sampling policy for storing the routing headers/decision chain (we don't want to store full chain for 100% of free-tier requests), (2) how to represent fallback confidence/metrics (why fallback: capacity vs quality vs quota).
Mina: propose sampling rules: enterprise: 100%, paid-tier: 25%, free-tier: 5% default. Allow customer override via console toggle per-org. We already have per-org telemetry flags.
Toby: for fallback reason, we can store a short enum in the header (capacity|latency|quota|policy). Keep it as a 1-2 token code to keep logs small. Example payload in trace metadata: 
```
{"decision_path": ["policy:route_by_tier","check:capacity(false)","fallback:variant=rwv-1-q4","reason:capacity"], "fallback_code":"capacity"}
```
Kendra: in the UX show human-friendly text for enums and a link to the policy block that fired. Also add a small cost delta estimate when a fallback happened (e.g., "saved ~0.6c/token vs default variant"). That helps product teams assess impact.
Mina: caveat — cost delta is best-effort and must be approximate. We'll compute it from per-variant token cost table and the response token count in the trace. Mark as estimate.
Jorge: privacy/compliance check: any concerns with storing more detail in traces? Toby?
Toby: as long as we don't dump prompt text or PII into the decision chain it's fine. Decision headers are metadata only. We'll add a truncation/PII-scan guard in the ingest pipeline, and ensure it's opt-out for orgs with strict retention settings.
deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: routing-headers-telemetry v2 -> eng-platform-canary at 22:00 UTC.
Jorge: action items: (a) eng-platform to add header -> trace mapping + sampling config (Mina), (b) console to add badges + side-panel playback (Kendra/ConsoleUX), (c) telemetry team to add fallback_code enum and cost-estimate field (Toby). I'll open tickets.
Kendra: I'll add a tiny copy spec for the hover tooltip (1-2 lines + link to policy).
Mina: I'll start the backend PR and include feature flag: routing_rationale_ui. Target: canary next week. :thumbsup:
Jorge: thanks — let's keep the trace id visible in the side-panel so SREs can jump to full logs.
ConsoleUX-Bot: noted — include `trace_id` link, sampling indicator (sampled / not-sampled), and a timestamp of when the decision chain was evaluated.
Toby: cc @security for retention defaults — we'll keep decision metadata retention aligned with existing trace retention by org.
Jorge: great. If no objections I'll file the RFC and break into tickets.
Kendra: no objections.
Mina: filing PR draft shortly.
Jorge: done, PR/Tickets: https://redwood.internal/r/PLAT-8342 (RFC), https://redwood.internal/t/ENG-4421 (backend), https://redwood.internal/t/UX-1298 (console).
